THE APPLICATION U/S 239 CRPC FILED ON BEHALF OF ACCUSED/REVISIONIST BIRENDRA NATH GHOSH Birendra Nath Ghose And Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28802604/

AND SULEKHA RANI GHOSH AND DIRECTING FRAMING OF CHARGES U/S 498A/406/34 IPC AGAINST THEM.

ORDER:
1. Revisionists have filed present revision petition challenging the impugned order dated 25.09.2024 whereby Ld. JMFC(Mahila Court)-04 West had dismissed their application for charge and directed framing of charges against them under Sections mentioned above.
2. Revisionists Birendra Nath Ghosh and Sulekha Rani Ghosh are the accused no. 2 and 3 respectively before Ld. Trial Court.
One other accused namely Saroj Kumar Ghosh is accused no. 1 before Ld. Trial Court but he has not challenged the impugned order on charge.
3. Complainant before Ld. Trial Court is impleaded as Respondent no.2 while State is impleaded as Respondent no.1.
For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred to by their nomenclature before Ld. Trial Court.
4. Arguments on the revision petition heard.
Record carefully perused.
Reply filed by respondent no.2 and written submissions filed on behalf of the revisionists are also perused.

BRIEF FACTS:
5. Brief facts of the case are that complainant is the wife of accused no.1 Saroj Kumar Ghosh.
Accused no.2 Birendra Nath Ghosh and Accused no. 3 Sulekha Rani Ghosh are the parents in law of the complainant.
The present FIR was registered on 28.07.2020 u/s 498A/406/34 IPC on the basis of a complaint dated 24.02.2020 made by the complainant before ACP CAW Cell.
After appearance of the accused persons and compliance of Section 207 CrPC, arguments on the point of charge were heard by Ld. Trial Court.

Revisionists also filed an application u/s 239 CrPC seeking discharge which was dismissed by Ld. Trial Court vide impugned order dated 25.09.2024 and charges u/s 498A/406/34 IPC were directed to be framed against all the accused persons.

GROUNDS OF REVISION:
6.
In the present revision petition, the impugned order has been challenged on the ground that charges have been framed against the revisionist without there being any material against them on record.
The charges have been framed merely on the basis of a complaint and statement of the complainant recorded u/s 161 CrPC which is not an admissible evidence in itself.

The bills of jewellery placed on record are dated 04-05 years prior to the date of marriage pointing towards the falsity of the allegations made in the complaint regarding giving of those jewellery articles to the complainant in marriage.
The application of the revisionist u/s 239 CrPC for discharge has been dismissed without any sufficient reason.
The entire material on record, even if taken to the gospel truth is not sufficient to make out any prima facie case against the accused persons.
Moreover, Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate the fact that the present FIR was registered after filing of a divorce petition by accused no.1 and was thus, an afterthought.

Accordingly, discharge of the Birendra Nath Ghose And Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28802604/
2 revisionists/accused no. 2 and 3 and setting aside of impugned order is sought.

sentences.text: 7. Ld.

Counsel for the revisionists has relied upon the decisions of the Apex Court in Payal Sharma Vs State of Punjab cited as 2024 SCC Online SC 3473 and Priti Gupta Vs State (2010) 7 SCC 667 wherein under similar facts, the FIRs registered u/s 498A IPC were quashed.

ARGUMENTS OF RESPONDENT:
8.
Per contra, a detailed reply has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2.
Revision is also vehemently opposed on behalf of State as well as complainant/Respondent no.2.
It is submitted that the impugned order is a well reasoned order passed on the basis of material available on record and evidences produced along with the chargesheet.
There is no illegality or perversity pointed out by Ld. Counsel for the revisionist in the impugned order.
The impugned order is a detailed order and cannot be interfered with by the present revision petition as revisional court has limited jurisdiction.
Unless the lower court has exceeded its jurisdiction or there is any perversity pointed out in the impugned order, the same cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction.
There are detailed statements of the complainant and her father recorded during investigation which clearly make out prima facie case against both the revisionists.
The allegations are also accompanied with bills of jewellers and photographs of articles given in dowry.
Some of the jewellery has also been seized during investigation.

Merely because the jewellery was purchased few years prior to the marriage, it is not sufficient to doubt the fact that the said jewellery was given in marriage as it is a general practice that parents start collecting jewellery for their daughters much prior to fixing of their marriages.

The decisions relied upon by Ld.
Counsel for the revisionist are not applicable as they are distinguishable on facts and passed on the basis of peculiar facts of those particular cases.

It is submitted that once the allegations have been made by the complainant and witnesses during investigation in their statements u/s 161 CrPC and they reflect prima facie commission of offences, charges have to be framed and opportunity has to be given to the prosecution to prove the allegations and the accused persons cannot be discharged merely because statement of complainant u/s 164 CrPC has not been recorded.
In these circumstances, dismissal of the present revision petition is sought.
9. I have heard the submissions made and carefully perused the record.

10. The scope of enquiry, a judge is required to make while considering the question of framing of charges has been considered by the Apex Court in Union of India Vs.
Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4.

entities.text:
Union of India Vs.
Prafulla Kumar Samal and Anr. (1979) 3 SCC 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After an exhaustive survey of the case law on the point, the Apex court has laid down the following principles:-
" (1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for Birendra Nath Ghose And Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28802604/
3

entities.text: Birendra Nath Ghose And Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.

(2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained the Court will be, fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.
(3) The test to determine a prima facie case would be naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application.

By and large however, if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.

(4) That in exercising his jurisdiction under section 227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and experienced Judge cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouth-piece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.

This however,
does not mean that the Judge should make a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial."

11. I have carefully perused the complaint on which present FIR has been registered as well as the documents annexed with the chargesheet and the statements of witnesses recorded u/s 161 and 164 CrPC.
12.

Considering the overall material available on record, no infirmity or illegality is found in the impugned order dated 25.09.2024 whereby charges were directed to be framed u/s 498A/406/34 IPC against the revisionists in addition to accused Saroj as prima facie case for offences under those sections is reflected from the material available on record.
The order dated 25.09.2024 is a detailed and well reasoned passed after considering all the materials and allegations against various accused persons.

A bare perusal of the order dated 25.09.2024 clearly shows that it has not been passed in a routine manner but after considering the allegations and evidence against each and every accused persons and categorically dealing with the grounds of discharge put forth by the revisionists herein in their application u/s 239 CrPC.
13.

No infirmity, illegality or perversity in the impugned order has been pointed out by Ld. Counsel for the revisionists either during the course of arguments or in the grounds for revision mentioned in the petition nor the same is observed by this Court.

The statements of witnesses recorded u/s 161 CrPC have to be considered while passing an order on charge and the same cannot be ignored on the ground that statement u/s 164 CrPC has not been recorded as there is no such mandate of law.

As regards the contentions of Ld. Counsels for the revisionists that the present FIR was got registered by the complainant after filing of divorce petition against her by her husband, the same can also not be made a ground for doubting the allegations made in the complaint and statements u/s 161 CrPC.

Ld. Trial Court has gone deeply into the allegations against both the revisionists and has rightly Birendra Nath Ghose And Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28802604/
4 dismissed their application for discharge holding that prima facie case u/s 498A/406/34 IPC was made out against both the revisionists as essential ingredients of those offences are reflected from the statement of the complainant recorded during investigation.
14.

Counsel for the revisionists

they cannot be made a ground for discharge in the present case as in those matters, FIR has been quashed on the basis of peculiar facts of those cases.
15. In view of the reasons given above, I find no merit in the present revision petition.
The same is accordingly, dismissed and the impugned order dated 25.09.2024 is upheld.
16. TCR be sent back along with a copy of this order.
17. Revision file be consigned to Record Room after completion of all legal formalities.
